transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Ava M. (Redwood AE), Liam C. (Redwood SE), Samir P. (Redwood Partner Ops); Priya N., Jorge R., Ellen P., Tom B. (Starlite Cloud)
Recording link: (internal) https://redwood.zoom/rec/xxxxxxxxx

Summary:
Quick partner intro between Redwood and Starlite Cloud to explore integration options: marketplace listing, dedicated GPU capacity resale, and VPC-connected private deployments. Discussed technical constraints (networking, peering, KMS), typical SLAs, and next steps to schedule a technical deep-dive and exchange infra docs.

Topics covered:
- Redwood partner program overview and partner tiers
- Integration patterns: marketplace + API vs dedicated co-managed nodes vs private (VPC/on-prem)
- GPU SKU mapping (T4, A10, A100, H100) and quantization/perf tradeoffs
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS integration, audit logs retention
- Pilot scope, success criteria, and timelines

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on — super excited for this intro between Redwood and Starlite. Quick intros?
[00:10] Priya Nair: Hi all, Priya here, partnerships at Starlite. We run marketplace and partner ecosystem stuff.
[00:15] Jorge Ramirez: Jorge, head of infra at Starlite Cloud. I look after the GPU clusters and network.
[00:20] Ellen Park: Ellen, solutions architect, I'll be the technical contact.
[00:24] Tom Becker: Tom, product for GPU offerings.
[00:27] Liam Chen: Liam, I'm the SE on the Redwood side, I work on integrations and perf.
[00:31] Samir Patel: Samir, partner ops — mostly commercial and enablement questions.
[00:35] Ava Martinez: Awesome. Agenda — quick partner program overview, then walk through integration patterns and constraints, then next steps. Sound good?
[00:41] Priya Nair: Yep sounds good.

[02:05] Liam Chen: To start, Redwood's partner program has three typical integration models — 1) marketplace listing where you resell or refer Redwood hosted API, 2) dedicated capacity where partners host or reserve GPUs and we route customer workloads, and 3) private deployments — VPC peering or on-prem for regulated customers. We often mix modes per customer.
[02:35] Tom Becker: When you say dedicated capacity, do you mean we run Redwood runtime on our infra and customers talk to us?
[02:42] Ava Martinez: Two variants — either Redwood manages a 'dedicated' pool in our Dedicated product but behind your billing/channel, or you run Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) in your environment. For reseller scenarios, we have an option where we onboard partner-managed pools that we route to with signed agreements.
[03:02] Jorge Ramirez: Ok — what about network topology? We're staunch about private peering for enterprise customers.
[03:10] Liam Chen: We support VPC peering and privateLink style endpoints. For Redwood Private we can do customer-managed networking entirely within your VPC; for marketplace/dedicated there is an option for secure tunnels and peering. Note: some customers want all traffic to never leave their VPC, that's Private.
[03:32] Ellen Park: How does auth work for that model — SSO, tokens, KMS?
[03:38] Liam Chen: We integrate with SAML/SSO for control plane, and for data-plane keys we support KMS/HSM integrations. Customers can bring their own keys (BYOK) in Private deployments; for Dedicated we offer KMS integrations and audit logs.

[05:10] Priya Nair: From a go-to-market perspective, our partners care about margins and ease of onboarding — what docs or enablement do you provide?
[05:18] Samir Patel: We have a partner enablement kit — deck, integration checklist, pricing matrix, and a technical onboarding repo. We'll share those after the call (Ava).
[05:26] Priya Nair: Great. Also, are there any certification levels for partners?
[05:30] Ava Martinez: Yes — bronze/silver/gold based on joint bookings, enablement completed, and technical vetting. There's an advanced tier for partners who can run Redwood Private fully.

[07:12] Tom Becker: Technical Q: what runtimes do you support? Our customers ask for H100 and A100; support for quantized models matters to cost.
[07:20] Liam Chen: We support a wide matrix — T4/A10 for lower cost, A100/H100 for high perf. We have quantized execution paths and recommend INT8/4-bit for many workloads. Caveat: quantization changes accuracy — we provide guidance and eval tooling via Redwood Optimize.
[07:45] Tom Becker: Do you provide perf baselines? Like tokens/sec for A100 vs T4 for various sequence lengths?
[07:51] Liam Chen: Yes — we'll share a perf spreadsheet and some sample benchmarks. For partners we can provide per-SKU perf numbers, but they vary by model, seq length, batch size. I'll prepare an example for T4 vs A100 with and without quantization.

[10:00] Jorge Ramirez: Network egress cost — customers want to keep costs low. If we route through Starlite do we see double egress charges?
[10:10] Ava Martinez: We can architect to minimize egress. For Private deployments there's no public egress; for Dedicated we can use peering to avoid public egress where possible. We'll need to map region-to-region flows to be precise.

[12:35] Ellen Park: Security — SOC2, penetration testing, audit logs retention?
[12:40] Liam Chen: Redwood is SOC2 Type II. We maintain audit logs and can export them to your SIEM. Retention is configurable depending on plan. For Private deployments customers retain full control; for Dedicated we have enterprise options for longer retention. We'll attach our SOC2 summary.
[13:05] Priya Nair: Do you support SAML for partner-level access — like partner admin portal?
[13:10] Samir Patel: Yes, partners get an admin portal with RBAC, SAML SSO, and per-tenant billing views.

[15:00] Tom Becker: On the integration side: do you have an SDK or do partners need to integrate at REST level?
[15:06] Liam Chen: We provide REST and SDKs (Python/Go/Node). For partners integrating with marketplace we'll provide example connectors and a lightweight agent for routing.
[15:24] Jorge Ramirez: Is there a lightweight runtime we can run on edge boxes?
[15:29] Liam Chen: We have a slim inference runtime for edge cases but most partners run full nodes for tenancy. For very latency-sensitive customers we support co-location options.

[18:15] Ava Martinez: Pricing model — for marketplace referrals it's usage-based revenue share; for Dedicated there are reserved commitments with escalators; for Private there's a licensing fee plus support. We'll share high-level pricing matrix.
[18:33] Priya Nair: Do pilots have minimum commits?
[18:37] Samir Patel: Pilots are usually low-friction — we do a 60-90 day pilot with test credits or a small reserved pool so we can demonstrate perf and economics.

[20:50] Ellen Park: Deep dive question — how does Redwood handle KV cache / prefix caching? We want to avoid repeating prefixes across calls to reduce cost.
[20:58] Liam Chen: We have automatic KV caching and prefix cache strategies — the runtime keeps warm KV shards and we can configure TTLs. Sometimes transcription shows KV cash or K-V cache, but it's the same. There's also a sticky routing option to keep sessions on the same host for cache hits.

[24:12] Tom Becker: Any constraints around multi-tenancy and noisy neighbors?
[24:18] Liam Chen: In Dedicated we allocate GPU pools per partner/customer and we use QoS and batch isolation. For hosted there are limits and auto-throttling. For mission-critical customers we recommend Dedicated or Private to avoid noisy neighbor issues.

[28:00] Jorge Ramirez: From our side, we have custom networking policies and strict egress rules. We'll need a network runbook and specific firewall ports.
[28:08] Ava Martinez: We'll provide a runbook template and network requirements doc. We'll also work through the peering and route tables with your infra team.

[30:20] Priya Nair: Commercially we also want co-marketing and listing in your partner marketplace, any lift on Redwood side?
[30:28] Ava Martinez: Yes — partners get marketplace placement, joint case studies on qualified deals, and co-marketing credits for gold-tier partners.

[33:00] Ellen Park: For the tech deep-dive, we'd like to focus on: 1) deployment topology for Dedicated, 2) KMS integration flow and BYOK, 3) performance baselines for H100/A100 with 4-bit quantization.
[33:16] Liam Chen: Happy to run that. We'll bring perf benches and a reproducible test harness. We'll also try to simulate your region map so we can estimate egress.

[36:50] Tom Becker: Legal questions — what does the contract look like for reseller vs private? Do we have revenue share splits?
[36:58] Samir Patel: We have templated partner agreements; reseller revenue share depends on tier and volume. For Dedicated/resale there's usually a margin per-usage plus potential upfront commitment. We'll loop in legal post-intro.

[39:10] Priya Nair: Any integration references we can start with?
[39:15] Ava Martinez: I'll share the partner enablement repo: github.com/redwood/partner-onboarding and a partner_deck link. Also perf spreadsheet: docs.redwood.ai/partner-perf-template.xlsx

[41:00] Jorge Ramirez: Onboarding timeline — if we wanted to pilot in January what's realistic?
[41:08] Ava Martinez: If we get infra docs this week and schedule the tech deep-dive early Jan, a small pilot in mid-late Jan is feasible. The pilot would be 6-8 weeks to collect perf and SLO telemetry.

[44:20] Ellen Park: Do you have reference partners with similar scale?
[44:26] Ava Martinez: Yes — we can introduce you to two partners who run dedicated pools and one who runs Redwood Private. I'll ask for permission and make intros.

[47:45] Tom Becker: One nit — latency SLOs. What's your typical p50/p95 for hosted vs dedicated?
[47:52] Liam Chen: Hosted p50 is typically sub-200ms for many seq lengths; p95 depends on batching and model size; Dedicated and Private offer tighter SLOs — we can hit sub-100ms p50 for optimized runtimes on H100 with tuned kernels. We'll provide sample dashboards from Redwood Console.

[50:00] Priya Nair: Ok let's recap next steps?
[50:05] Ava Martinez: Recap: Ava to send partner deck, partner enablement repo, perf spreadsheet, SOC2 summary by 2026-12-23. Liam to prep tech deep-dive slides and perf samples for T4/A100/H100 and quantized runtimes, propose dates for week of Jan 4. Jorge to share infra diagram, current GPU SKUs by region by 2026-12-27. Priya to confirm internal stakeholders for commercial.
[50:35] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[50:38] Jorge Ramirez: Thanks.
[50:40] Tom Becker: Appreciate it.
[50:42] Ellen Park: Thanks everyone.
[50:45] Samir Patel: We'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.

[53:00] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (eg 'Redwood Dedikated' or 'K-V cash' instead of KV cache). References to shared artifacts: partner deck (link in email), integration repo (github.com/redwood/partner-onboarding), perf spreadsheet (docs.redwood.ai/partner-perf-template.xlsx).
